curator.name: 세인트존스 칼리지
curator.description: 미국 메릴랜드주 아나폴리스와 뉴멕시코주 산타페에 캠퍼스를 둔 리버럴 아츠 칼리지다. 1696년 킹 윌리엄 스쿨로 문을 열어 1784년 세인트존스 칼리지로 인가받았고, 1937년부터 고전 원전 읽기를 뼈대로 삼는 그레이트 북스 교육과정을 운영한다. 전공을 나누지 않아 전교생이 같은 원전 목록을 같은 순서로 읽으며, 교수 대신 튜터라 부르는 교원이 이끄는 20명 미만 토론 수업이 수업의 중심이다.
curator.description_en: St. John's College is a liberal arts college with campuses in Annapolis, Maryland and Santa Fe, New Mexico. Founded in 1696 as King William's School and chartered as St. John's College in 1784, it adopted its Great Books curriculum in 1937. The college has no majors: every student reads the same original texts in the same order and discusses them in seminars of fewer than 20 students, led by faculty who are called tutors rather than professors.

list.title: 세인트존스 고전 목록
list.title_en: St. John's College Great Books Reading List
list.description: 세인트존스 칼리지 학부생이 4년간 읽는 원전 목록이다. 1학년 그리스 고전에서 출발해 2학년 성서·중세·르네상스, 3학년 근대, 4학년 19~20세기로 이어지며 문학·철학·정치·수학·자연과학·음악을 한 줄기로 다룬다. 순위 없이 학년별로만 나뉜다.
list.description_en: The list of original texts that St. John's College undergraduates read over four years. It moves chronologically from Greek antiquity in the freshman year through scripture and the medieval and Renaissance worlds in the sophomore year, early modernity in the junior year, and the 19th and 20th centuries in the senior year, treating literature, philosophy, politics, mathematics, natural science, and music as a single sequence. It is unranked and organized only by year of study.
list.method: 학과와 전공을 두지 않고 전교생이 같은 원전을 정해진 순서로 읽는 필수 교육과정이다. 1937년 도입 이후 목록은 계속 바뀌어 왔다. 출처 페이지는 학년별로 저자 카드를 늘어놓고 각 카드에 작품과 주제 분류를 붙여 보여주며, 3·4학년 선택 수업에서만 읽는 책도 같은 목록에 표시 없이 섞여 있다. 출처 페이지 스스로 최근 변경, 한쪽 캠퍼스에서만 읽는 책, 일부만 읽는 책, 3·4학년 선택 수업 도서 때문에 현재 목록과 정확히 일치하지 않을 수 있다고 밝힌다.
list.method_en: A required, non-elective core curriculum: with no departments or majors, all students read the same texts in the same order. The curriculum was adopted in 1937 and the list has been revised continuously since. The source page presents author cards grouped by year of study, each card naming the work(s) and subject tags, with books read only in junior and senior elective classes mixed into the same lists without any marker. The page itself states that it 'may not accurately reflect the current reading list due to recent changes, works that are read only on one campus, works that are read in part, and works that are read by some students as junior and senior elective classes.'

collection_report.structure: The primary source page divides the list into four sections by year of study (Freshman, Sophomore, Junior, Senior). Each section is a flat sequence of author cards; every card carries an author heading, a 'Work(s)' line naming one or more works, and 'Subject(s)' tags. The page holds 270 author cards in total: 34 Freshman, 43 Sophomore, 98 Junior, 95 Senior. Individual works were split out of those cards to produce the items above, and each item's note records the year of study of its card.
collection_report.gaps: Subject tags (Literature; Mathematics; Natural Sciences; Philosophy, Theology, and Psychology; Classical Studies and Greek; History and Social Science; Music; Language) appear on the source page but are not stored here. The junior and senior sections mix required seminar readings with elective-class readings and the page marks no boundary between them, so a 'Junior year' or 'Senior year' note cannot be read as 'required seminar text'. Non-book entries were kept as printed because the source lists them as readings: Alfred Hitchcock 'Selected movies', Edouard Manet 'Art', Igor Stravinsky 'Music', and musical works (operas, quartets, symphonies, masses). Eight cards carry no work title at all - Hebrew Bible, New Testament, The Bhagavad Gita, Daode jing, The Rise and Decline of the Roman Republic, Neuroscience (Junior), Neuroscience (Senior), United States Supreme Court Decisions - and for these the card heading was used as the title with the creator left null.
collection_report.uncertainties: 1) The alphabetical companion page (great-books-reading-list-glance) prints different titles for several science texts than the main page: Cannizzaro is 'Sketch of a Course of Chemical Philosophy' there but 'Letter to Professor S. De Luca' on the main page, and Fahrenheit, Gay-Lussac, Lavoisier, Berthollet, Black and Avogadro differ likewise. The main page wording was used throughout, since the task designates the Reading List page as primary. 2) Roughly thirty works appear twice, once under Junior and once under Senior (Arendt, Camus, Feynman, Garcia Marquez, Gibbon, Hardy, Henry James, Laozi, Laxness, Lorenz, Borges, Ibn Majah, Manet, Piketty, Proust, Rilke, Russell, Shakespeare, Spengler, Stravinsky, Voltaire, Zhuangzi, Woolf, Joyce, Chopin, Hurston, Naipaul, Gaddis, Duchamp, de Sevigne, Neuroscience). Both copies were kept because the source lists both. 3) Four cards bundle several works inside a single italic span with no separator in the markup and remain as one item: Sophocles 'Antigone, Philoctetes'; James Baldwin 'Stranger in the Village, The Fire Next Time'; Flannery O'Connor 'Good Country People, Revelation, The Displaced Person'; Virginia Woolf 'To the Lighthouse, A Room of One's Own'. They were not split on commas because titles such as Faulkner's 'Go Down, Moses' and Foucault's 'Security, Territory, and Population' contain commas of their own. 4) Six cards whose markup did not map onto titles were resolved by reading the printed text: Shakespeare (Sophomore; trailing 'and Sonnets' outside the italics), Leibniz (Junior; 'Essay on Dynamics' and 'Philosophical Essays' not italicized), Wordsworth (Junior; only '1799' italicized), Gwendolyn Brooks (Senior; 'Sonnets from Children of the Poor'), Hans Spemann (Freshman; the parenthetical '(Nobel Lecture 1935)' folded into the title), and United States Historical Documents (Junior; three documents in plain text, split into three items with creator null). 5) The source gives no publication year or edition for the list itself, so published_year and edition are null; per-work publication years are not printed on the page and are null for every item. 6) Author names are printed inconsistently on the source page and were left exactly as printed: 'Soren Kierkegaard' (Junior) versus 'Soren Kierkegaard' with the slashed o (Senior), 'Madame de Sevigne' versus 'Madame de Sevigne' with an accent, 'Tennesee Williams', 'Ranier Maria Rilke', 'J.J. Thomson' versus 'J. J. Thomson'. 7) The page does not say which works belong to the Annapolis campus and which to Santa Fe, so no campus attribution is recorded; the college's separate per-campus seminar schedule pages were not consulted.
